title: Chicken Teriyaki
subtitle: pan-fried chicken with a sweet soy glaze
excerpt: Chicken teriyaki is a Japanese weeknight classic. Bone-in chicken thighs are pan-fried until the skin is crisp, then glazed in a sweet and savoury sauce of soy, honey, and mirin. It comes together in under 30 minutes.
sourceNotes: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking technique where food is grilled or broiled with a glaze of soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. The word comes from teri (lustre) and yaki (grilled). It has been part of Japanese home cooking for centuries and became popular worldwide in the late twentieth century.

content.text: Teriyaki is one of the most useful Japanese cooking techniques to learn. The glaze is made from just three ingredients -- soy sauce, mirin, and a sweetener -- and it works on chicken, fish, and tofu. Chicken thighs are the best cut here because they stay juicy even if slightly overcooked.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, mirin, garlic, and ginger in a small bowl. This is the teriyaki sauce.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken skin-side down. Cook for 6 to 7 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip the chicken. Cook for another 5 minutes until cooked through.
Pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, turning the chicken to coat. The sauce will thicken and become glossy.
Rest for 2 minutes, then slice and serve with steamed rice.

items.symptom: Sauce burns before the chicken is cooked
items.cause: Pan too hot when the sauce is added
items.fix: Reduce heat to medium before adding the sauce. Keep stirring and turning the chicken so it coats evenly without scorching.

content.text: Teriyaki is one of Japan's most recognised cooking methods. The technique produces a deeply savoury, slightly sweet glaze that clings to the meat. Chicken thighs work better than breast here -- they stay juicy. Serve with plain rice and pickled vegetables.
